source_refs.note: Topic 4.1.1.3 List Operations (PDF 93-95, printed 90-92), as printed: eight code blocks; curly quotes, the stray quote and wrong Output, and the printed names insertf(), append!), popO, indexO are marked.

blocks.text: Let's explore some common operations we can perform on a list using real-world examples and Python code.

items: Insertion: Adding a new item to your list is like adding a new task to your to-do list. You can insert an item at different positions in the list. Here are several ways to do this:
Inserting at a Specific Position: You can insert an item at any position in the list using the 'insertf()' function.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints 'insertf()'; the list function is insert(), as the code below uses.

party_list = ["Buy drinks”, “Buy decorations", "Buy snacks", “Buy cold drinks "]
party_list.insert (0 ’ , “Invite friends”) # add Invite friends at start
print(party_list)
# Output: ["Buy drinks, “Buy decorations", "Buy snacks", “Buy cold drinks "]
book_errors: # Output: ["Buy drinks, “Buy decorations", "Buy snacks", “Buy cold drinks "]

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: As printed this code does not run: curly quotation marks (“ ” ’) stand where Python needs straight quotes, and a stray ’ follows the 0; Python stops with SyntaxError: invalid character '“' (U+201C). Written correctly: party_list = ["Buy drinks", "Buy decorations", "Buy snacks", "Buy cold drinks "] and party_list.insert(0, "Invite friends"). The printed Output also leaves out "Invite friends"; the program prints ['Invite friends', 'Buy drinks', 'Buy decorations', 'Buy snacks', 'Buy cold drinks '].

items: Appending to the End: If you want to add an item to the end of the list, use the 'append!)' function.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints 'append!)'; the list function is append(), as the code below uses.

party_list = [“Invite friends”, "Buy cold drinks”, “Buy decorations", "Buy snacks",]
party_list.append ("Order cake”) # Adds ’Order cake’ at the end
print(party_list)

# Output: [’’Invite friends’’, ‘’Buy cold drinks’’, ’’Buy decorations’’, ‘’Buy snacks’’, “Order cake”]

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Curly quotes again: “Invite friends”, "Buy cold drinks” followed by “Buy decorations", and "Order cake”. Python stops with SyntaxError: invalid character '“' (U+201C). With straight quotes the program prints ['Invite friends', 'Buy cold drinks', 'Buy decorations', 'Buy snacks', 'Order cake'], as the Output comment says.

items: Extending the List: You can also add multiple items at once using the 'extend()' functions.

blocks.text:
party_list = ["Invite friends", "Buy decorations ", "Buy snacks”, "Buy cold drinks"]
party_list.extend(["Party hats", "Streamers"]) # Add multiple items at once
print(party_list)
# Output: [’’Invite friends’’, ’’Buy decorations’’, ‘’Buy snacks ‘’, ‘’Buy cold drinks’’, ’’Party hats’’, ‘’Streamers’’]

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: "Buy snacks” ends with a curly quote, so Python does not see the string end and stops with SyntaxError: unterminated string literal. With "Buy snacks" the program prints ['Invite friends', 'Buy decorations ', 'Buy snacks', 'Buy cold drinks', 'Party hats', 'Streamers'].

items: Deletion: Removing an item from your list is like crossing off a task you've completed. You can remove items in various ways
Removing by Value: Use the 'remove()' function to delete the first occurrence of a specific item.

blocks.text:
party_list = ["Invite friends ","Buy decorations”, "Buy snacks”, "Buy cold drinks"]
party_list.remove ("Buy snacks”) # Removes ’Buy snacks ’ from the list
print(party_list)
# Output: [’Invite friends’, ’Buy decorations’, ’Buy cold drinks ’]

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: "Buy decorations” and "Buy snacks” end with curly quotes; Python stops with SyntaxError: invalid character '”' (U+201D). With straight quotes the program prints ['Invite friends ', 'Buy decorations', 'Buy cold drinks'].

items: Removing by Index: Use the 'popO' function to remove an item at a specific index.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints 'popO'; the list function is pop(), as the code below uses.

party_list = ["Invite friends ", "Buy decorations", "Buy cold drinks " ]
party_list.pop (0) # Removes the item at index 0
print(party_list)
# Output: [’Buy decorations’, ’Buy cold drinks’]

items: Removing All Items: Use the 'clear()' function to remove all items from the list.

blocks.text:
party_list = ["Invite friends" , "Buy decorations", "Buy cold drinks " ]
# Removes all items from the list
party_list.clear ()
print(party_list) # Output : []

items: Searching: Finding an item in a list is similar to looking for a specific task in your to-do list. You can search for an item using different functions:
Checking for Existence: Use the 'in' keyword to check if an item exists in the list.
Finding the Index: Use the 'indexO' function to find the position of an item in the list.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints 'indexO'; the list function is index(), as the code below uses.

party_list = ["Invite friends", "Buy decorations", "Buy cold drinks " ]
index = party_list.index("Buy decorations") # Finds the position of ’Buy decorations’
print("Index of ’Buy decorations’:", index)
# Output: Index of ’Buy decorations’: 1
